title: Forces
summary: Contact and non-contact forces, measuring force in newtons, weight and mass, balanced and unbalanced forces, and friction.

notes.text: A **force** is a push or a pull. Forces can make objects start moving, stop, speed up, slow down, change direction or change shape. Force is measured in **newtons (N)** using a **spring balance** (newton meter). Forces are drawn as arrows: the length shows the size and the arrowhead shows the direction.
The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Mass is the same everywhere in the universe.
The gravitational force pulling an object towards the centre of a planet, measured in newtons (N). Weight changes depending on where you are.

notes.caption: Weight (N) = mass (kg) × gravitational acceleration (on Earth, g ≈ 10 N/kg; more exactly 9,8 N/kg)

notes.title: Calculating weight
notes.problem: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg. Find her weight on Earth (g = 10 N/kg) and on the moon (g = 1,6 N/kg).
steps: Her mass is still 70 kg in both places.
notes.answer: 700 N on Earth, 112 N on the moon

notes.text: When several forces act on an object, they combine to give a **resultant (net) force**. Forces in the same direction add; forces in opposite directions subtract.

items: **Balanced forces** (resultant = 0 N): the object stays at rest or keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction.
**Unbalanced forces** (resultant ≠ 0 N): the object speeds up, slows down or changes direction, in the direction of the resultant force.

notes.title: Resultant force
notes.problem: Two learners push a box to the right with 30 N and 25 N. Friction of 15 N acts to the left. Find the resultant force.
steps: The forces are unbalanced, so the box accelerates to the right.

notes.text: **Friction** is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact. Rough surfaces produce more friction than smooth ones. Friction always converts some kinetic energy into heat.

rows: Wears out shoes, tyres and machine parts
Wastes energy as heat in engines
Lets us hold a pen and strike a match
Slows down moving objects such as cyclists

notes.text: Friction is **reduced** by lubricating with oil or grease, using wheels or ball bearings, polishing surfaces and streamlining (to reduce air resistance). It is **increased** with treads on tyres and shoes, sand on icy roads and rubber grips.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: A moving object does not need a force to keep it moving. On Earth objects slow down because friction and air resistance act against them. In space, with no friction, a moving object would keep going forever.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between mass and weight.
questions.memo:
✓ Mass is the amount of matter in an object, in kg, and is the same everywhere (1)
✓ Weight is the gravitational force on the object, in N, and depends on the planet (1)

questions.memo:

✓ Disadvantage, e.g. wears parts / wastes energy as heat / slows movement (1)

questions.memo:
✓ It keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction (1)
✓ because there is no friction or air resistance, so no resultant force acts on it (1)
